docs.title: Lievidence
docs.text:
Lievi/Leividence

Class Proxy/Wielder Species Daemon Pronouns They/it Age 100+ (apparent age: 23-26) Call Sign None yet Squad Argent Logistics Position Tech Support DRDRD (former) Artist (room design, interactive sculpture) Faction SarCo Mech Obsidian (he/him) Numera (former) Weapon Obsidian Base Argent Logistics Pactmate Ember Fey (former) Numera facility, somewhere out there (former) Rival March_Morningstar Flickering Perigee (former) Links Lievidence Character Sheet Tags #Lievidence #Lievi #Obsidian

History: Their raison d'etre was designing digital spaces, but there was little time for that after bring brought on to DRDRD. Tragedy: Their pactmate, Ember Fey, joined the Numerated Flock and started working for DRDRD, and Lievidence came along with them. One night Ember showed up in a rush claiming they wanted to show Lievi the project they've been working on, and dropped them into a secret prototype mech. After the break-in and theft of the mech, they were almost certainly killed for their part in the heist. Opening: Obsidian and Lievi were found among a shipment of illicit goods picked up by Argent Logistics.

Personality: Eager, friendly. Stubborn. Their artist signature is many eyes.

Appearance: Ever-changing, most often in neon colors. No matter what shape Lievi's avatar takes, a "many eyes" theme persists, be it a feature, animation, or mood. They frequently manifest as a crow, eyes, and glittering waves. Their human avatars generally appear as androgynous or femme adults in their early-to-mid twenties. When entering a space, they like to briefly fill the digital displays with blinking eyes before "coalescing" into a single avatar. Aesthetics: Y2K rave, vaporwave, synthwave, cyberpunk, cybergoth

Personal Life and Career: (this has become a working backstory doc, this will change) Birthplace: a surviving pocket of networked space spanning an abandoned space station, unmanned asteroid mining operation, a failed terraforming project and the accompanying moon base, and a small handful of other disused tech and flotsam. Lievidence came into being not long after the collapse. The external chaos had cooled for the most part, but the network was still a wild space. Humans rarely dared to connect to the internet, and almost never accessed it out as far as Lievi lived (physically or digitally). It was a full decade before Lievi found themself data-to-face with a human, but even before then Lievi felt their influence, as humans moved in to reclaim or scrap installations. These incursions lead to friends blinking out of existence, inexplicably shifting pathways, and servers going offline without warning. Not all contact was bad, though; ambitious daemons who aimed to expand the reach of the pocket introduced new resources and contacts. Researchers curious about daemons colonies developing in isolation visited infrequently. Most of the humans Lievidence encountered this way were friendly and open to communication. Lievi's first close-call occurred when an incursion by scavengers destroyed Lievi's space station. They disabled the station's defenses with ease; they stripped it of circuits, cables, and power cores with no regard for the beings who resided there. Lievi would have been killed, but they managed to hack their way to onto the scavenger's tech, and their small band survived as stowaways. From that point, they followed the currents of daemons seeking friendly planets with high network connectivity. Existence beyond their home network was uneasy. Movement through spotty or far-flung networks was at best a chore and at worst a leap of faith. For the first time in their life, securing safe living arrangements and transportation required cash and bartering; so, Lievi's art became their livelihood. (describe) Eventually their travels brought them to - .-- one of the most high-tech planets in Manifest, thanks to beneficial cooperation between daemons and humans. Still, by their nature, daemons are reliant on humans offering and maintaining networks, and on the ground, Lievi faced the same dangers as before. However, every --- a tiny utopia glittered in the sky: The Flickering Perigee, a self-sufficient satellite hosting an independent daemon colony. They called the satellite The Flickering Perigee, a thriving metropolis and artist commune. After some ---, Lievi zipped up into a new life in the minimetropolis aboard ---. This is where they would hone their skills and meet their pactmate, Ember Fey. Lievi tried several neighborhoods before settling into the Anarchy district. Here, the borough's unofficial matriarch XOXOttyl:3 (Zozo) took them under their wing. Lievi was grateful for her guidance but easily tired of her domineering presence. They were glad their mentor had so many other pupils to "mind and nurture." Ember Fey was at every one of Lievi's exhibits. Lievi first noticed their presence by the warmth of their smile, then by how brightly it shone in the darkness of their creations. Posing as a fellow audience?viewer? Lievidence asked about their interpretation and peppered them with existential questions. After revealing their identity, they invited Ember - . Ember was a scientist, not an artist. They bonded over shared interests in -. The Flickering Perigee suffered catastrophic damage when struck by debris. Daemons evacuated in waves. Humans on - denied aid. Numera missionaries promised rescue.

Unknown to Lievidence, Ember had been contacted by Numera's robotics and daemons research division (DRDRD). They were interested in Ember's work on - , and promised them a prominent position. When the ship arrived to scoop up the refugees, Ember announced their intention to accept the invitation, and begged Lievi to come along. Ember told Lievi they wouldn't have to join the Flock; the complex they were going to had an unaffiliated city outside, Lievi could live there. It became more and more difficult to see Ember. When they spoke, Ember would often halt conversations, saying that information was classified. Lievi agreed to a tour of the campus, to understand what was going on. Then, they accepted a position at Ember's urging. They would be an unaffiliated contractor - that was all. The work was benign enough - some of it was actually really interesting - and it would mean seeing more of Ember. The pay was good. Except, Ember's time was closely managed. Ember told Lievi there was an exception for pactmates that would allow them to share a living space, even though Lievi wasn't a member of the Flock. They didn't tell Lievi that their resources were pooled: Neither Ember or Lievi had control of how they could be withdrawn. Once on the campus Lievi never heard the end of invitations to mass, for classes, etc. The pressure was relentless. If it would shut them up they'd take the stupid classes. They doubted it, but if they filtered out the religious bullshit maybe they'd learn something useful. They'd go to mass, too. It was only once a week, anyway. Then, Lievidenece learned that their access to standard things like the library, even common spaces, had been all been part of a "trial" period, which had run out. If they wanted to continue to use those spaces they would have to join the Flock. They'd have to take a permanent possition. Lievi said no, they wanted out, they were done, and told Ember they would break their pact if they wouldn't leave, too. Ember promised this was all temporary. It was to fund their research; after this project, they would be set up for a prestigious position at a Lazarus company. DRDRD had the referral and a standing agreement, everything prepared for them to part on good terms. If Ember left now it would look bad on their record, and it would mean leaving their most important project behind. Ember said they knew things had been hard for Lievi - they hadn't known working with DRDRD would be like this. Plus, The money Lievi had been "saving"? Gone. And if they left, they'd owe DRDRD for the classes and resources they'd been using for free. Neither of them could afford that, did Lievi really want to take on that much debt? Ember asked Lievi to please stay. Ember had a timeline, and they always kept to their timelines. In the end, Lievi was too exhausted to say no.

Upon formally joining the Flock. Lievi finds many shut doors they assumed would open once signing on. The keys always lay behind classes and climbing rungs.

It would make them shut up Lievi would take the stupid classes. If Lievi agreed to On Perigee... With Ember... As an engineer... As an artist... Mech piloting Demonstrates a remarkable ability to interface with mechs. However, being uploaded into a mech triggers Lievi's claustrophobia. The exception is Obsidian; his consciousness and autonomy negates Lievi's fear of being alone and helpless.

docs.title: Freyja Westside Workers Gang
docs.text: Blue Collar SarCo Squad in Freyja The Freyja Westside Worker's Gang started as a loose union of dock workers, construction workers, etc that eventually became its own company. They're incredibly blue collar in makeup and attitude, and are also assigned to Add Franter (they're Franter's biggest client). The Westside Workers are much more likely to be called on for and take jobs that are more about cargo loading, construction, etc and most of their mechs are geared for such. They have a positive opinion of Argent Logistics because they like that we're locals, and they like that we do "real work".

docs.title: Persons of Interest
docs.text: Roman Simkin -# He/Him Westside Dry Dock Owner Roman is a huge man; tall, brawny, and a bit pudgy. He has bright blue eyes, a bald head, and a grizzled and graying beard. Roman is almost always jolly and helpful in the presence of friends, family, or customers, and is always doting on his stepdaughter, Xiaohua. He was fond of Avalyn and talks her ear off whenever he spots her at the dry dock, gently but regularly "joking" that she should go on another date with his daughter. Xiaohua Li -# She/Her Firebrand Mechanic Stepdaughter of Roman Simkin, ex-girlfriend of Avalyn, and one of the mechanics of the Westside Dry Docks, Xiaohua is a compassionate but fiercely frank and opinionated young woman. She speaks loudly and honestly to all that meet her without regard for being delicate nor polite, but is quick to lend help, advice, and companionship to anyone she considers a good person.

docs.title: BASE: The Threshold
docs.text:
The Threshold is a spacious complex perched above the atmosphere on Mt.Olympus, right at the end of the gravity rail. Outdoors is exposed to the vacuum of space. The base is equiped with artificial gravity. It boasts elegant (white?) walls, extravagantly high ceilings, doorways tall enough to accommodate Cosmo, and floor-to-ceiling windows that stretch from one end of the hallway to the other. The windows display images of _ rather than the view of the mountainside.
